occurrence_result.reason_summary: The target occurrence "薛瑩" appears in Liu Xiaobiao's annotation as "薛瑩後漢書曰..." — i.e., Xue Ying is named as the author of the "Hou Han Shu" (後漢書) from which the quoted material about Li Ying (李膺) is introduced. The occurrence itself identifies the source/author of the cited work, which is the definition of citation_source.

The target occurrence 齊桓公 appears in Liu Xiaobiao's annotation quoting the Shiji: "管仲夷吾者潁上人相齊桓公九合諸侯一匡天下." Here 齊桓公 is the ruler whom Guan Zhong served as minister. The occurrence identifies the historical ruler in the biographical description of Guan Zhong drawn from the Shiji. It does not function as speaker, addressee, citation source (the citation source is the Shiji itself, not 齊桓公), historical exemplum (the exemplum being invoked is Guan Zhong/管仲, not 齊桓公), genealogy, collective, or attribute. It is a plain reference to a historical person within the quoted source material.

The target occurrence "滔" (Fu Tao) appears in the Liu annotation text: "滔宻以啓温" — Fu Tao secretly reported to Huan Wen. In this occurrence, Fu Tao is an active participant in the narrated event (secretly informing/reporting to Huan Wen). He is not the speaker of the quoted utterance, not an addressee, not a citation source, not a collective, not an attribute expression, and not a genealogy reference. He is simply an actor in the narrated sequence described in the annotation. The subsequent full-name mention "伏滔" in the same annotation further confirms he is being described as acting within the narrative context.

The target occurrence "王師" (imperial army) is a collective entity denoting the Jin dynasty government forces. The frozen identity confirms semantic_kind is "collective" and reference_type is "descriptive_reference." The occurrence appears in Liu Xiaobiao's annotation quoting 晉陽秋, stating that the imperial army was defeated at Jiangshan. The occurrence itself denotes a collective entity (the government troops), which fits the collective_reference function directly. It is not a participant in a specific narrated event beyond being the collective subject of the defeat statement, and no more specific function (speaker, addressee, citation_source, etc.) applies.

The target occurrence "字景真" (courtesy name Jingzhen) is the courtesy-name attribute expression for 桓亮 (Huan Liang). The frozen identity confirms attribute_type="courtesy_name" with attribute_value="景真" and bearer_hint="桓亮". The occurrence itself expresses an attribute (the courtesy name) of the bearer 桓亮, which fits the person_attribute function definition: "the target occurrence itself expresses an attribute or value of a bearer." The annotation text "續晉陽秋曰桓亮字景真" introduces the courtesy name as an attribute of Huan Liang.

The target occurrence "嘏" (Fu Gu) appears in the Liu annotation text: "傷嘏問曰婦人才色並茂為難子之聘也遺才存色/燕婉歷年後婦病亡未殯傅嘏往喭粲粲不明而神". Here 嘏 (Fu Gu) is an active participant in the narrated event — he asks a question (問曰) about the wife's talents and beauty, and later goes to offer condolences (往喭) to Xun Can. The occurrence is not functioning as speaker (he is not the speaker of the current utterance being quoted in the main text), not an addressee, not a citation source, not a historical exemplum, and not a genealogy reference. It is a person actively participating in the narrated events of the annotation. The full name 傅嘏 later in the same annotation confirms this is the same person acting in the narrative.

The target occurrence 簡文 (Emperor Jianwen) at the start of the main text is the subject who sits in the dark room and summons 宣武 (Huan Wen). The occurrence actively participates in the narrated event—sitting, summoning, and later responding. No more specific function (speaker, addressee, citation_source, etc.) applies to this particular occurrence at the beginning of the sentence; it is the actor in the narrated scene.

The target occurrence "上" (referring to 簡文/簡文帝) appears in the phrase "問上何在" where 宣武 (桓溫) asks where the emperor is. The target is the object of the question "where is the emperor?" — it refers to 簡文 as the person being asked about, not as a participant performing an action in the narrated event, not as speaker/addressee (宣武 is the speaker asking, and 簡文 is not directly addressed here), and not as a citation source, exemplum, attribute, collective, or genealogy reference. The occurrence simply refers to/describes the entity 簡文 within the question. Thus it functions as a reference.

The target occurrence "某" (referring to 司馬昱/簡文) appears within the utterance "某在斯" spoken by 簡文 in response to 宣武's question "上何在". The referent 簡文 is the speaker of this quoted utterance, and "某" is his self-reference inside that utterance. The discourse context confirms speaker_hint=簡文 and self_reference_hint=某. Thus the occurrence functions as speaker self-reference.

The target occurrence 宣武 (Huan Wen) appears in the main text: 簡文在暗室中坐召宣武宣武至問上何在簡文曰某在斯. Huan Wen is summoned (召宣武), arrives (宣武至), and asks where the emperor is (問上何在). He actively participates in the narrated event as the summoned person who arrives and poses the question. The discourse context identifies 簡文 as speaker and 宣武 as addressee hint, but the target occurrence itself is not the speaker's self-reference nor a vocative/direct address—it is the narrative subject performing actions (arriving, asking). No more specific function (speaker, addressee, citation_source, exemplum, etc.) applies to this occurrence itself. Therefore it functions as a participant in the narrated event.

The target occurrence "吾" (I/me) is the first-person self-reference used by 庾道季 (Yu Daoji), who is identified as the speaker at the start of the utterance ("庾道季云..."). The pronoun "吾" is the speaker's self-reference inside his own quoted speech, functioning as the speaker of the current utterance.

庾道季 (Yu Daoji) states that in terms of thought and principle harmony, he is ashamed before 康伯 (Kang Bo, i.e., 韓康伯). The target occurrence 康伯 is the person being compared/assessed within the speaker's utterance. He is not the speaker, not the addressee, not a citation source, not a historical exemplum invoked as background comparison, and not a genealogy reference. He is the object of the speaker's self-assessment—actively the referent of the narrated comparison. No more specific function applies, so participant is the correct classification.

The target occurrence "文度" (Wang Tanzhi) appears in Yu Daoji's utterance where he compares himself to Kangbo and Wendu in terms of reasoning and willpower. Wendu is the person being compared/assessed within the narrated content of the utterance. He is not the speaker (Yu Daoji is), not the addressee (no direct address), not a citation source, not a historical exemplum invoked for comparison to the current discourse, and not a genealogy reference. He is an entity actively involved in the narrated evaluation being expressed — the person against whom the speaker measures himself — making him a participant in the narrated event.

The target occurrence "庾道季" (Yu Daoji) is immediately followed by "云" (says), identifying him as the speaker of the utterance that follows. The discourse context confirms speaker_hint "庾道季" and self_reference_hint "吾" (I/we) used within the quoted speech. The target occurrence itself identifies who speaks the utterance, making it a speaker occurrence.

The target occurrence "身" (self) appears in the Liu annotation quoting 鄧粲晉紀: "上身服儉約" (the emperor himself wore frugal clothing). The referent is 司馬睿 (元帝), the emperor. The occurrence "身" functions as an emphatic self-reference to the emperor within the quoted historical narrative of the Jin Annals. It does not mark a speaker, addressee, citation source, exemplum, genealogy, collective, or attribute expression. The emperor is described as wearing frugal clothing — "身" here is the subject performing/being described, not an attribute expression itself. Since the occurrence refers to the emperor within the narrated historical content without a more specific function, it is best classified as reference.

The target occurrence "帝" (the Emperor, i.e., 元帝) appears in the Liu annotation text: "王導深以諌帝乃令左右進觴飲而覆之" — Wang Dao earnestly remonstrated with the Emperor, and the Emperor then ordered his attendants to bring a cup, drank, and overturned it. The Emperor is the recipient of Wang Dao's remonstrance and the agent who orders the attendants and drinks. He actively participates in the narrated event. He is not the speaker (Wang Dao is), not directly addressed/vocatively identified (he is the object of 諌, a remonstrance verb, not a direct address), not a citation source, not an exemplum, and not an attribute or genealogy expression. Therefore the narrative function is participant.

The target occurrence "帝" (the Emperor, i.e., 元帝) appears in the main text: "元帝過江猶好酒王茂弘與帝有舊常流涕諌帝許之命酌酒一酣從是遂斷". The Emperor is an active participant in the narrated events: Wang Maohong (王茂弘) had an old friendship with him, tearfully remonstrated with him, and the Emperor agreed and ordered wine to be poured, drinking deeply and thereafter stopping. The occurrence "帝" refers to the Emperor as an active participant in the narrative events (being remonstrated with, agreeing, ordering wine). It does not function as speaker, addressee, citation source, exemplum, genealogy, attribute, or collective reference. It is not merely a reference since the Emperor actively participates in the narrated events.

The target occurrence "元帝" (Emperor Yuan) at the start of the main text is the subject who "過江" (crossed the Yangtze) and "猶好酒" (still loved wine). He is an active participant in the narrated event — the story recounts how Emperor Yuan crossed the river, continued drinking, was admonished by Wang Maohong (王茂弘), and then stopped drinking. The occurrence directly participates in the narrative action rather than serving as speaker, addressee, citation source, exemplum, or any other more specific function.

The target occurrence "殷荆州" (Yin Jingzhou, i.e., 殷仲堪) appears in the main text where 顧長康 (Gu Kaizhi) wants to paint a portrait of him. The occurrence identifies the person whom Gu wishes to depict — the object of the action "欲圖" (wants to paint). Yin Zhongkan is an active participant in the narrated scene: he is the person being painted and subsequently responds in dialogue ("殷曰我形惡不煩耳"). The occurrence functions as a participant in the narrated event, not as speaker (the speaker is 顧長康 per the discourse context, and Yin's own speech follows later with the separate 殷 mention), not as addressee (Gu's statement is not directly addressing him in a vocative sense), and not as citation source or exemplum. The office title "荆州" is used as a reference form for the person, but the narrative function is participation in the event of being painted.

The target occurrence "明府" (an honorific for a prefect/governor) is used by 顧長康 (Gu Kaizhi) when directly addressing 殷仲堪 (Yin Zhongkan). In the text, 顧 says "明府正為眼爾" — "Prefect, it is precisely because of your eyes" — which is a direct vocative address to Yin Zhongkan within the quoted speech. The discourse context confirms addressee_hint is 殷仲堪, and the speaker is 顧長康. The honorific "明府" functions as a direct address to the recipient of the utterance, making it an addressee occurrence.

The target occurrence "顧" is the surname reference at the start of the main text, beginning "顧長康好寫起人形欲圖殷荆州..." This is the opening of the narrative where Gu Kaizhi (顧愷之/顧長康) is introduced as the subject who likes to paint human figures and wants to paint Yin Jingzhou. The occurrence functions as the participant actively involved in the narrated event (the desire to paint Yin). It is not a speaker occurrence at this point (the first 顧 is in the narrator's framing clause, not in direct speech), not an addressee, and not performing any more specific function. The antecedent hint confirms this is the same person as 顧長康 mentioned at the start.

The target occurrence "我" is the first-person pronoun used by 殷仲堪 (殷荆州) in his own direct speech: "殷曰我形惡不煩耳". The discourse context confirms speaker_hint is 殷仲堪 and self_reference_hint is 我. This occurrence is the speaker's self-reference inside his own utterance, identifying who is speaking. Therefore it functions as speaker.

The target occurrence "周侯" appears in the clause "謝幼輿謂周侯曰" where 謝幼輿 addresses 周侯 (周顗). The verb 謂...曰 marks direct speech directed at 周侯, making him the recipient/addressee of the utterance. The discourse context confirms speaker_hint: 謝幼輿. The occurrence itself identifies the speaker of the current utterance, so it functions as speaker.

The occurrence identifies the person Zhou Yi within the annotation's explanatory gloss. It does not mark a speaker, addressee, citation source, exemplum, genealogy, collective, or attribute.
